chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:

About the man who needs to relieve himself while he is in prayer, so he said: 'He gestures with his head and indicates with his hand and glorifies (God); and the woman, when she needs to relieve herself while she is praying, she claps with her hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way for men and women to break their prayer to relieve themselves according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the juristic principle that minor bodily needs do not invalidate the prayer, allowing for a 'gesture' (ishara) rather than a full exit. It highlights the classical Shia distinction in non-verbal communication during prayer, where men use subtle head and hand movements while women use hand clapping, reflecting the scholarly view that these actions do not constitute speaking or laughing, which would break the prayer.
